attempts.summary: On node1, cron access is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (cronie honors cron.allow as an exclusive whitelist when present, and pre-existing /etc/cron.deny was empty so it plays no role). Created the opsadmin user, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin, and verified enforcement both before and after a full node reboot: unlisted users are rejected by `crontab` ("not allowed to use this program"), while opsadmin and root can still create/read crontabs. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol with boot_id proof of an actual reboot and post-restart re-verification of crond health and the cron access restriction.
